question: to the Commission Ana Catarina Mendes (S&D) Subject:

Since 2016, the Commission has funded, through the Horizon Europe programme, a series of successive projects that have helped combat disinformation: InVID, followed by WeVerify, and most recently Vera AI. These projects have enabled the development of free and opensource tools designed to help journalists, fact-checkers, and civil society groups verify the authenticity of online content. These tools allow users to detect disinformation, identify the use of deepfakes in social media posts, and uncover illegal or deceptive behaviour using artificial intelligence. They are widely recognised as a successful outcome of the Horizon Europe programme and of the Commission’s efforts to support the development of tools to combat disinformation. However, as the Vera AI project nears its conclusion, it appears that no new call for proposals has been planned to ensure that this essential work can continue. This raises concerns about the sustainability of such tools. 1.

Can the Commission explain why no new funding is currently planned to support the continued development of these tools, which have proven to be effective and are developed independently by civil society groups?
What is the Commission’s strategy to ensure the future availability of free, reliable and European-made solutions to tackle disinformation?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.5.2026) Safeguarding the integrity of the information space to support everyone in society to access reliable and trustworthy information and exercise their democratic rights is essential for democracy as outlined in the European Democracy Shield (EDS) Communication1. In this vein, the Commission has supported the development of technological tools that enable journalists, fact-checkers, civil society groups and all citizens to detect disinformation and foreign interference (FIMI) campaigns, including through support for consecutive projects under Horizon 20202 and Horizon Europe3 such as InVID4, WeVerify5 and vera.ai6, with around EUR 34 million through EU Horizon Europe Cluster 4 funding. Results developed under vera.ai are being further taken up by some members of the consortium in the ongoing AI-CODE project, which ensures continuity of tools and expertise supported through earlier EU funding. Furthermore, the Commission also supports other relevant projects contributing to information integrity, such as European Narrative Observatory pilots, recurring funding to foster media literacy under Creative Europe, and support to the European Digital Media Observatory (EDMO) under Digital Europe7. As part of the EDS, the Commission has also launched new initiatives, such as a call for proposals for a common research framework8 that will support technical infrastructure and research on information integrity. This is complemented by support for a European Network of Fact-Checkers. Europe must be better equipped to protect the integrity of its public debate and democratic processes. For that reason, under the new Multiannual Financial Framework, the Commission proposes to continue supporting innovation across the media sector. As part of the proposed
1 Communication on the European Democracy Shield:
new AgoraEU programme9, the Commission intends to step up support actions that promote and protect a free, viable and diverse EU information ecosystem.
9 Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing the 'AgoraEU'
programme for the period 2028-2034, and repealing Regulations (EU) 2021/692 and (EU) 2021/818: https://eurlex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025PC0550.
